key_insight: Publicly available policies at U.S. osteopathic medical schools rarely gave clear, scenario-specific support for patient-information decisions, even when relevant guidance could be found.
clinical_relevance: For educators and policy teams, the study suggests that accessible institutional guidance may not be enough unless it directly maps to real-world decision scenarios.
method: Exploratory vignette-based document analysis across 20 U.S. osteopathic medical schools
Eight patient-information vignettes created 160 school-vignette pairs
Three AI-assisted retrieval/evaluation runs per pair, with investigator review of discordant ratings
evidence_signal: Among 160 school-vignette pairs, final ratings were mostly Ambiguous (82.5%); only 13.1% showed sufficient support (Explicitly Supported or Inferable).
watch_item: This was a nonprobability sample with AI-assisted classification, so results may not generalize to all schools or reflect how policies are applied in practice.
paper_title: Decision Support in Publicly Available Patient Information Policies at U.S. Osteopathic Medical Schools: A Vignette-Based Document Analysis
